claims.text: Hybrid Monte Carlo sampling is a data-driven method for determining optimal HEA compositions.
Hybrid Monte Carlo sampling can efficiently identify refractory HEA compositions that are intrinsically strong, ductile, and low in weight.
The initial material-design space contains multiple principal elements and a very large selection of possible compositions.
Hybrid Monte Carlo sampling is applied to the alloy-design problem.
The proposed method is intended for high-temperature operating conditions.
The HEA composition space is the structural mediator affected by the sampling intervention.
Combining molecular-dynamics simulations with machine-learning techniques can predict optimal alloy compositions.
The predicted compositions will have improved strength.
The predicted compositions will have improved ductility.
The predicted compositions will have low weight.
Strategies for quickly determining optimal HEA compositions are currently lacking.
The vast HEA composition space creates a need for efficient sampling methods.
The effectiveness of Hybrid Monte Carlo sampling depends on the simulation time step.
The effectiveness of Hybrid Monte Carlo sampling depends on temperature.
The effectiveness of Hybrid Monte Carlo sampling depends on the number of sampling iterations.

contradictions.description: The proposed method is identified as Hybrid Monte Carlo sampling, but the stated mechanism is a combination of molecular dynamics and machine learning; the hypothesis does not explain whether or how these components constitute or integrate with HMC.
